evidence.clarity: 1440 first screen: H1 'See your proof before we staple.' plus subhead 'prints zines and art books for independent artists, 25 to 500 copies, from your print-ready PDF' and a red 'Upload your PDF' button; what, who and next step are all there. The one muddying element is the hero status line 'Sheet 1 of 6, outside: pages 24 and 1. 24 + 1 = 25...', which is printer's arithmetic a stranger meets before knowing why it matters.
evidence.fit: Reads as made by people who run a press: imposition sheet with crop, fold and registration marks, a K step wedge, a docket table (Step/Who/What/When), a galley with proofreader's strike and caret marks against copy shops and big printers, and a saddle-stapler drawing. Price ($2.10 x 50 = $105.00 job ticket), the no-full-bleed limit (hero note, red cover marks, closing line) and the 120-artists fact without names are all handled. No clipping or overlap at 1440, 768 or 390 in any state I drove (sheet 6 inside, 64pp, error states). The left hero column is dense at 1440: CTA, note, readout and seven controls stacked under the headline; the sheet's page art is crude flat black rectangles.

evidence.interaction: 1440/768/390: Turn over (animated flip, instant on keyboard Enter), Next/Previous wrap correctly, +4/-4 redraws, Reset returns to 24pp sheet 1 outside. evidence.copy: Specific and in the trade's vocabulary: 'printer's spread, not a reading spread', 'the one place your facing pages print side by side, so art can cross the fold here', 'The caret ‸ is the proofreader's mark for insert here'. Buttons say what they do. Slightly heavy on imposition explanation for a buyer who just wants good printing; the hero arithmetic line is the least readable sentence on the page.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 and 390: specific outcome (see a proof before binding, 25-500 copies, from $2.10, two working days), a labelled sample proof in view, and an 'Upload your PDF' action that goes where it says. The sample is a schematic dummy, so it makes the process believable more than the print quality.

problems: The hero artifact demonstrates imposition rather than print quality; the illustrator's main doubt (will it look better than the copy shop) is answered only in words.
Hero left column at 1440 is crowded: CTA, note, status readout, stepper and four sheet buttons compete under the headline.
The hero status line '24 + 1 = 25, like every side of every sheet' is insider arithmetic that a first-time visitor reads before the page explains it two sections later.

evidence.clarity: 1440: H1 'See your zine come off the press before we staple a single copy.' with lede 'We print zines and art books in runs of 25 to 500. Upload a print-ready PDF, and within two working days we post a photo of your proof...' and two labelled buttons ('Upload your PDF', 'Check your PDF first'). A stranger can repeat it exactly; nothing later contradicts it.
evidence.fit: The PDF checker is a deliberate answer to 'usually on a laptop with their PDF open': it reads the visitor's own file in the browser and fills a job ticket. Job ticket, rubber stamp and red-pencil proof marks give press flavour, pricing is published for the base job with 'Priced at upload' for anything else, and the full-bleed limit is enforced in the ticket. The overall rhythm (split hero, three-step row, price block, closing band) leans closer to a SaaS landing page than a press.
evidence.distinctiveness: Product-specific pieces exist: the halftone proof illustration with 'solids even' red pencil, the run-size ruler (25-500 vs 'Big online printers start here'), the stamped ticket. They sit inside a familiar structure: split hero, 'How a job moves' three-column steps, comparison, price card, closing CTA. On this renderer the display stack falls back to a heavy generic sans, which further flattens the identity.
evidence.proof: The checker genuinely works: I loaded a 24-page A5 PDF ('24 pages in the file. Pages are A5, our standard size.'), a 22-page PDF with a bleed box (flags multiple-of-4 and full-bleed cover), and an A5 spreads file (detected as spreads). It answers 'will my file work and what will it cost'. But it starts at y≈1456 at 1440 and y≈2234 at 390, i.e. the third screen; the hero image is a static illustration.
evidence.craft: Navy-on-paper palette is coherent and the ticket rows are well built. Defects: the display fallback (heavy wide sans here) with very tight leading makes the 768 headline lines nearly touch; the 'Ready to upload' and 'Fix 3 things' stamp renders very pale, and the probe reports a serious colour-contrast node; 11px labels in the hero SVG; at 1440 the check section has a large empty area under the drop zone before a file is chosen; at 390 the rotated stamp hangs over the ticket's left border.
evidence.mobile: 390: stacks cleanly, no overflow; the header keeps only 'Upload a PDF' (150x40) with How it works / Check your PDF / Prices hidden and no menu to reach them. Inputs are 41px, the size select 35px and the ink/cover choice buttons 37px tall, under 44. The checker is the third screen down (drop zone at y 2234, stamp at y 3434). evidence.honesty: The hero illustration is captioned 'A proof from our own test zine. We don't have permission to show the work we print for artists, so this sheet is ours', which is visible at 1440 but below the first viewport at 390, and calls an SVG drawing a proof. The checker says up front 'Your file stays on your computer... sends nothing to us. You'll choose the file again on the upload page.' CTA goes to the supplied URL. A boxed 'What we can't do yet' list is honest but reads as a disclaimer section.
evidence.interaction: All ticket fields respond live with row icons and written notes (copies 10 -> 'Our smallest run is 25 copies'; -5 -> 'Enter a whole number'; 99999 -> 'Our largest run is 500 copies'; 22 pages -> 'Add 2 blank pages to make 24'). Non-PDF upload gives a clear message. Bug: after loading the spreads PDF and then notes.txt, the Pages row still says 'Your PDF is set up as two-page spreads' for a file that is no longer loaded. No reset control. Keyboard reaches file input, fields and radios with visible focus. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Plain and specific: 'You probably have the file open already', 'They want 1,000 copies, and you see your zine for the first time when the boxes arrive', 'The upload page asks for the same details, so keep this ticket open'. Error messages are written, not defaulted. 'For the runs nobody else wants to print well' is a strong line. Steps section repeats the hero lede nearly word for word.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, two accurate actions, and a captioned proof illustration in view. 390: H1, lede and both buttons fit, but only the top edge of the illustration shows and its caption is off-screen, so nothing in the phone viewport backs the promise; the real artifact (checker) is not in the first screen at either width.

problems: The strongest piece, the PDF checker, sits two to three screens down; the hero shows a static illustration and at 390 almost nothing in the first viewport supports the promise.
Mobile execution: no way to reach section nav on the phone, ticket controls under 44px (select 35px, choice buttons 37px), stamp overhanging the card edge.
Type and contrast: generic heavy fallback display face with cramped leading (768 headline), pale stamp text flagged by the probe, and stale spreads error after loading a different file.

reason: A has a clear point of view that comes from running a press, puts an operable, honestly labelled proof in the first viewport at every width, and holds up in every state I drove, including the mobile menu. B has the more useful tool (a real in-browser PDF check), but it is buried below the fold inside a more templated, less refined layout. If the buyer's main doubt were 'will my file work' rather than how the page earns trust in the first screen, B's checker could outweigh A's craft.
